title: Rockefeller, CARE, Red Cross, Colombo Plan, MDGs, SDGs, Alma-Ata and Astana

steps.title: Rockefeller Foundation and Indian public health
steps.tx: The **Rockefeller Foundation** seeded modern public health philanthropy: hookworm and yellow fever campaigns, schools of public health, and in India support that helped establish the All India Institute of Hygiene and Public Health, Calcutta (1932), alongside malaria and medical education work. Its model (demonstration, training, handover to government) taught foundations to build institutions rather than run parallel services forever.
steps.say: Rockefeller money built institutions, including Calcutta's hygiene institute in 1932. Demonstrate, train, hand over: that was the model.

rows: All India Institute of Hygiene and Public Health 1932

steps.title: CARE: food and development NGO
steps.tx: **CARE (Cooperative for Assistance and Relief Everywhere)** began in 1945 shipping food parcels (the original CARE packages) to war torn Europe and evolved into a development organisation working on food security, nutrition, maternal health, and women's empowerment, including long running Indian nutrition and health programmes with state governments. Examinations pair CARE with food and nutrition relief origins.
steps.say: CARE started as food parcels in 1945 and grew into nutrition and women's development work. Food relief is its founding fingerprint.

nodes.label: Food aid expands to developing nations

steps.title: Red Cross and Red Crescent movement
steps.tx: The **Red Cross movement** unites the International Committee of the Red Cross (war and armed conflict protection under the Geneva Conventions), the International Federation (disaster relief and national society support), and national societies such as the Indian Red Cross Society (1920) running blood banks, disaster response, and first aid training. Its emblem is legally protected; misuse in conflict is a war crime.
steps.say: The Red Cross protects war victims, relieves disasters, and runs blood services. Its emblem carries legal protection.

steps.title: Colombo Plan: regional cooperation
steps.tx: The **Colombo Plan (1950)** organised cooperative economic and social development in Asia and the Pacific: richer members funded training fellowships, experts, and equipment for poorer members, with health manpower training a steady component. Headquartered in Colombo, Sri Lanka, it exemplifies South South plus donor cooperation that predates modern aid architecture, and examinations place it by year, city, and training mission.
steps.say: The Colombo Plan of 1950 funded fellowships and experts across Asia Pacific from Colombo. Training was its currency.

steps.title: Millennium Development Goals 2000 to 2015
steps.tx: The **Millennium Development Goals** set eight time bound targets for 2015 against 1990 baselines: three were directly health (goal four child mortality, five maternal health, six HIV malaria and other diseases), with poverty, education, gender, water, and partnership goals feeding them. India cut poverty and child deaths substantially yet missed maternal mortality pace, the honest mixed report card examiners expect.
steps.say: Eight goals, three directly health: children, mothers, and epidemics. India progressed well except on maternal pace.

steps.title: Sustainable Development Goals 2016 to 2030
steps.tx: The **Sustainable Development Goals** widened the frame to seventeen goals and universal (not only developing country) duties for 2030, with goal three (good health and well being) carrying thirteen targets including maternal mortality below seventy per hundred thousand, ending preventable newborn and child deaths, universal health coverage, and noncommunicable disease mortality cut by one third. Interlinkage (no goal alone) is the philosophy examiners quote.
steps.say: Seventeen universal goals to 2030; health is goal three with universal coverage inside. No goal succeeds alone.

steps.title: Alma-Ata declaration 1978
steps.tx: At Alma Ata (USSR, 1978) nations declared **primary health care** the key to Health for All by 2000: essential care scientifically sound, socially acceptable, universally accessible with community participation at affordable cost, built on eight elements from education and nutrition to essential drugs. India's National Health Policy 1983 domesticated Alma Ata. Its selective primary care critics (child survival packages) debated comprehensiveness for decades.
steps.say: Alma Ata 1978 made primary health care the road to health for all. Community participation and equity were its soul.

steps.title: Astana declaration 2018: PHC renewed
steps.tx: Forty years on, the **Astana declaration (2018, Kazakhstan)** recommitted the world to primary health care as the foundation of universal health coverage and the SDGs, adding empowered people and communities, multisectoral action, and integrated services with digital tools. Examinations pair Alma Ata (1978, health for all) with Astana (2018, universal health coverage) as bookends; confusing their years and slogans is the planted error.
steps.say: Astana 2018 renewed Alma Ata for the coverage era. 1978 promised health for all; 2018 promises coverage for all.

nodes.label: 1978 Alma Ata: PHC for Health for All

steps.title: Bilateral and voluntary agencies at a glance
steps.tx: Beyond the giants, **bilateral and voluntary health agencies** fill niches: USAID and DANIDA style bilateral aid tied to donor governments, the Ford Foundation (population and rural development in India), SIDA and DANIDA health sector support historically in Indian states, and professional voluntaries (Rotary's polio partnership with WHO and UNICEF). Polio eradication's partnership architecture is the model examination narrative of these actors combined.
steps.say: Bilaterals fund governments; foundations fund ideas; Rotary helped finish polio. Partnership architecture is the modern pattern.
